chunks: Al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) addressed the people in Mina and said: O people, whatever comes to you attributed to me which agrees with the Book of Allah, then I have indeed said it, and whatever comes to you opposing the Book of Allah, then I never said it.
ai.seo_question: How do we verify if a hadith is authentic based on the Quran?
ai.summary: This foundational hadith from Al-Kafi establishes the 'Mu'jizah' (miracle) of the Quran as the ultimate criterion for validating the Prophet's Sunnah, a principle central to Shia Usul al-Fiqh. It underscores that the Prophet's teachings are not independent legislation but are inextricably linked to the divine text, ensuring that any authentic tradition must align with the Quran's spirit and letter. This serves as a primary mechanism for distinguishing between genuine prophetic words and later accretions.
